newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to seek 1997 inflation below 10 pct - Dubinin.
newsitem.headline: Russia to seek 1997 inflation below 10 pct - Dubinin.

text.p: Russian currency policy will be directed to keeping inflation below 10 percent next year, Interfax news agency quoted central bank chairman Sergei Dubinin as saying on Wednesday.
Getting inflation to these levels would create conditions for real financial stability, he was quoted as telling a banking training conference.
"Our currency policy will be tied to this goal," he said.
Policy, which is currently being worked on in the government and central bank, would aim to make the exchange rate predictable over six months or a year, he said.
Prices from the beginning of this year to September 9 rose 16.2 percent. Year on year inflation in December 1995 was 131 percent.

Since the middle of last year the central bank has set upper and lower limits, known as a corridor, for the rouble, running for six months. For the current half year ending in December, it has set daily ranges providing for a gradual devaluation of the rouble.
Within this corridor the central bank sets daily buying and selling rates for its operations with major Russian banks.
